LESSON: READING 3.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we ensure we understand the events in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they retell the story in a few words using the five-finger

model.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner’s fluency skills are improved as they explain the events in the story from the beginning to the end in their

own words.

Values:
Respect: A learner accepts diverse opinions from peers during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem/confidence is enhanced as they creatively retell a story.

23

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies comprehension strategies in reading of texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
